name: Pari English Core
purpose: Compare candidate LLMs across research-backed English-language capabilities relevant to Pari before runtime, memory, quantization, or product routing are considered.
claimScope: Application-grounded multi-dimensional model selection; not a universal psychometric measure of one latent quantity called English ability.

researchBasis.designFramework: Evidence-Centered Benchmark Design (ACL 2024) + HELM-style multi-dimensional reporting
researchBasis.constructPolicy: Every dimension must be tied to a published linguistic/NLP construct or editing benchmark plus a Pari-specific shadow analogue.
researchBasis.weightBasis: product-prior, not a literature-derived psychometric scale
researchBasis.weightRationale: Lexical context and collocation are intentionally emphasized because Pari's primary interaction is contextual word/phrase replacement. Exact percentages are engineering priorities and must not be presented as empirically discovered constants.
researchBasis.sensitivityPolicy: Always report all seven dimensions and an equal-weight mean beside the product-weighted composite. If model ranking changes materially under equal weighting, treat the winner as weight-sensitive rather than universal.
researchBasis.contaminationBasis: Public benchmark results are separated from fresh shadow cases because benchmark contamination can inflate static benchmark scores; shadow cases test related constructs with new surface forms.
researchBasis.choiceOrderBasis: Forced-choice options are deterministically permuted and close contenders receive a two-presentation counterbalanced order test because LLM selection is sensitive to answer order/token position.
researchBasis.promptRobustnessBasis: Multi-prompt evaluation is required for close contenders because intent-preserving instruction paraphrases can materially change absolute scores and model rankings.
researchBasis.uncertaintyBasis: Small score differences require uncertainty reporting. Item bootstrap is supplemented by a two-level phenomenon/item hierarchical-bootstrap sensitivity analysis because author-written cases can share linguistic/template dependencies. Neither is interpreted as a universal-English confidence bound, and no universal minimum phenomenon count is asserted.
researchBasis.pairedComparisonBasis: Models evaluated on the same items are compared with paired item-level bootstrap rather than independent averages. Because shadow items are clustered by benchmark-authored linguistic phenomena, close-model comparisons also report a paired phenomenon/item hierarchical-bootstrap sensitivity lane. A directional robustness claim survives only when the item-level and hierarchical lanes agree; this agreement rule is a conservative Pari engineering policy, not a universal statistical law.
researchBasis.distributionBasis: Benchmark item mixtures are not assumed to be random samples from one universal real-world distribution; public-native, public-prompted, shadow, and product-use distributions are reported separately.
researchBasis.nativeProtocolBasis: Where a benchmark has a native/official protocol, that result is reported separately from Pari's common prompted adaptation. Prompted convenience scores must never be relabeled as official benchmark scores.
researchBasis.collocationProtocolBasis: EACL 2021 establishes the lexical-collocation retrieval/categorization construct and lexical-disjoint evaluation design, while SemanticQA ACL 2026 provides a modern LLM-facing 305-item LCC zero-shot protocol. These are related evidence sources but not interchangeable scores.
researchBasis.judgeBasis: Generative outputs must not be scored solely by one general-purpose LLM judge; use human references, deterministic metrics, official metrics, or independently human-validated specialized evaluators where possible.
researchBasis.metricDirectionBasis: Generative metric observations retain their natural direction and are transformed to utility only through the versioned english-core-generative-metric-contract.json; failure rates are never implicitly treated as higher-is-better.
researchBasis.sourcePinningBasis: Promotion-quality public benchmark runs pin immutable source revisions where tooling supports it and record resolved dataset fingerprints/library versions.
researchBasis.externalEvaluatorBasis: Promotion-quality SWORDS/JFLEG evidence pins the official evaluator checkout to a full Git commit, binds exact benchmark/reference/model-output bytes, executes the official evaluator directly, and archives evaluator code/output provenance instead of reimplementing the metric. SemanticQA LCC promotion builds bind the official dataset archive, prompt, taxonomy, task bytes and source commit; accuracy is the primary published LCC metric.
researchBasis.reproducibilityBasis: Promotion-quality runs must preserve enough model/runtime/task/scorer/source metadata to reproduce the result.

measures: controlled editing and generative English expression

composite.name: english_core_100
composite.rule: Always publish all seven subscores, the product-weighted composite, and the equal-weight dimension mean. This score must never replace Pari route-specific product acceptance.

lexical_context.researchConstruct: context-sensitive word meaning and lexical substitution

collocation_naturalness.researchConstruct: lexical collocation retrieval/classification, lexical-function semantics, and idiomatic compatibility
publicAnchors: SemanticQA 2026 LCC 8-category zero-shot (primary modern LLM anchor)

grammar_syntax.researchConstruct: linguistic acceptability and targeted grammatical phenomena

paraphrase_semantics.researchConstruct: structural/context-sensitive paraphrase equivalence under high lexical overlap

fluency_register.researchConstruct: holistic English fluency plus formality/register discrimination

generative_expression.researchConstruct: controlled text improvement, revision, paraphrasing, and restructuring

discourse.researchConstruct: discourse relation, temporal relation, coherence, and sentence ordering

evidenceLanes.publicNative: Benchmark-native/official protocols and source distributions where reproducible; highest-priority public evidence.
evidenceLanes.publicPromptedFull: Full locally scoreable public distribution under a common zero-shot prompted adaptation; adaptation must be named explicitly and source revision/fingerprint preserved for promotion use.
evidenceLanes.publicPromptedFast: Balanced/subsampled common prompted screen for inexpensive triage only.
evidenceLanes.freshShadow: Pari-authored fresh-surface diagnostic; currently author_labeled_unvalidated until independent annotation/adjudication.
evidenceLanes.robustnessDiagnostics: Prompt paraphrase, option-order counterbalancing, item/hierarchical uncertainty, protocol sensitivity and paired item-plus-phenomenon comparison; these diagnose evidence stability rather than adding another competence dimension.

evaluationProtocol.publicAnchorPolicy: Use official frozen evaluation splits and native/official evaluators where available. Never fine-tune on evaluation data.
evaluationProtocol.sourceRevisionPinning: Promotion-quality public builders must use immutable dataset revisions when supported and record resolved dataset fingerprints/library versions. Mutable default revisions are exploratory evidence only.
evaluationProtocol.shadowPolicy: Fresh Pari-authored cases are evaluation-only, rotated periodically, and must never be used for training or prompt optimization.
evaluationProtocol.shadowAudit: Run audit-english-core-shadow.mjs before model evaluation. Structural failures block the run; audit success does not validate linguistic gold labels.
evaluationProtocol.forcedChoice: Prefer direct A/B or label responses. Do not request explanations or chain-of-thought. Deterministically permute option order per case and record the permutation policy.
evaluationProtocol.choiceOrderRobustness: For close contenders, run the two-presentation counterbalanced option-order lane and report both-orders-correct, semantic-answer consistency and one-correct/one-wrong rates. This is a robustness gate, not a weighted score.
evaluationProtocol.choiceParser: Use the shared conservative JS/Python parsers so harmless answer wrappers are accepted consistently while free-form/multi-answer outputs remain invalid.
evaluationProtocol.probabilityScoring: When local runtimes expose token/logit probabilities reliably, record calibrated preference margins in addition to text-answer accuracy; do not silently substitute first-token scoring for observed text answers.
evaluationProtocol.nativeProtocolSeparation: Never relabel a common prompted adaptation as an official/native benchmark score. Report native, full-distribution prompted, and fast prompted lanes separately.
evaluationProtocol.collocationProtocolSeparation: Report SemanticQA 2026 prompted LCC separately from EACL 2021 supervised categorization/MLM retrieval. The former is the primary modern LLM selection anchor; the latter validates the construct and historical native protocol.
evaluationProtocol.generation: Use fixed task prompts and decoding settings per model class; preserve raw outputs.
evaluationProtocol.metricDirectionContract: Every required generative metric must exist in english-core-generative-metric-contract.json. Raw normalized observations preserve natural direction; lower-is-better metrics are inverted only by the scorer's declared utility transformation.
evaluationProtocol.judgePolicy: Official generative metric scores require structured metricProvenance. General-purpose LLM judges are secondary diagnostics. Specialist model judges require explicit human-validation evidence before entering the official composite.
evaluationProtocol.contamination: Report public-native/public-prompted and fresh-shadow results separately. A model with strong public scores but weak shadow scores is flagged for possible contamination/overfitting/protocol mismatch.
evaluationProtocol.runtimeSeparation: Latency, RAM, quantization and MTP are reported after English Core. They do not change the English competence evidence profile.
evaluationProtocol.sampling: Fast public subsets are engineering screens. Full/native benchmark metrics remain the authoritative public evidence for promotion/research reporting.
evaluationProtocol.weightSensitivity: Report both product-weighted and equal-weight composites and inspect per-dimension rankings before selecting a winner.
evaluationProtocol.multiPrompt: For close contenders, run the three-variant shadow robustness lane and report mean, worst-prompt, all-prompts-correct, answer consistency, and prompt spread. Never choose the best prompt after observing model results.
evaluationProtocol.uncertainty: Report per-dimension item-bootstrap intervals plus a two-level phenomenon/item hierarchical-bootstrap sensitivity analysis. Both are conditional on the current shadow construction; the hierarchical lane is explicitly exploratory because benchmark phenomena were deliberately designed rather than randomly sampled.
evaluationProtocol.pairedComparison: Use complete aligned paired comparison for close models. Report both paired item-bootstrap and paired phenomenon/item hierarchical-bootstrap sensitivity. Headline comparison requires identical benchmark/task hashes and full coverage. If the item interval includes zero, report inconclusive; if item and hierarchical directions disagree, report sensitivity_inconclusive rather than forcing a winner.
evaluationProtocol.distributionValidity: Do not interpret the shadow/public mixture as a random sample of universal English. Preserve per-source, per-dimension, per-phenomenon, and per-protocol views.
evaluationProtocol.modelFamilyAdaptation: Record base/instruct/chat checkpoint type and adaptation mode. Base models may use plain/native likelihood protocols; instruct/chat models should use their official chat template for prompted tasks where appropriate.
evaluationProtocol.promotionValidation: Before a promotion-quality comparison, run validate-english-core-run.py --promotion. Auto adaptation, unknown checkpoint/revision/quantization, missing artifact/task hashes, mixed adaptation modes or incomplete decoding/template provenance block promotion status.
evaluationProtocol.reproducibility: Promotion-quality runs record exact model/revision/artifact hash/quantization/runtime/task hash/decoding/template/hardware/source revision/fingerprint, official evaluator revision/code hash where relevant, and raw-output provenance.

promotion.englishCoreUse: Use the English Core profile and scoped composites to narrow Pari base-model candidates.
promotion.productUse: After English Core selection, run the existing Pari route-specific V1 acceptance suite.
promotion.hardRule: A high English Core score does not override semantic/safety veto failures in the product benchmark.
promotion.closeResultRule: A small observed lead without prompt/order robustness and paired item-plus-phenomenon statistical support is inconclusive, not a winner.
promotion.strongClaimGate: A strong cross-model English claim additionally requires primary native/official anchors, pinned public-source and official-evaluator provenance, prompt/order/protocol robustness, independently validated shadow labels, reproducibility metadata, and evidence that reasonable weighting choices do not materially reverse the conclusion.
